_about: Advisories that cover a pinned version but do not reach HID-Fi. Each says why, with the evidence, the date it was checked and what would make it reach us (revisit). An advisory that DOES reach HID-Fi is never listed here: it is fixed (AGENTS.md, 'Outside facts and dependencies'). Re-check every entry when the code it names changes.

GHSA-28hv-fwm3-rpcq.reason: WebServer Digest auth: HID-Fi never calls WebServer::authenticate()

GHSA-w887-pg2w-mfj2.reason: WebServer authenticate() bypass: HID-Fi never calls authenticate(); its own PIN gate is pinCheck()

GHSA-vqp8-ppw3-8mc7.reason: serveStatic() path traversal: HID-Fi has no file system and never calls serveStatic()
GHSA-vqp8-ppw3-8mc7.evidence: grep serveStatic hid_fi/ -> none; no FS partition used (docs/OTA.md)

GHSA-92j9-c75g-2c5f.reason: NetBIOS name_len: HID-Fi does not use the NetBIOS library (names come from mDNS)

GHSA-v7jh-c872-6jmp.reason: Vulnerable code is the HTTP_Server_AES_OTA_Update example, not the library; HID-Fi does not contain it
GHSA-v7jh-c872-6jmp.evidence: advisory text; no HTTPUpdateServer/Update upload handler in hid_fi/
GHSA-v7jh-c872-6jmp.revisit: a web upload handler for firmware - docs/OTA.md forbids an unsigned one

GHSA-3j8v-xgrq-5vg8.reason: esp_http_server WebSocket subprotocol: HID-Fi's WebSockets come from Links2004/arduinoWebSockets and its HTTP from Arduino WebServer, neither uses esp_http_server

GHSA-3pp8-42fh-3j3c.reason: Bluedroid AVRCP (Bluetooth Classic): the ESP32-S3 has no Bluetooth Classic, and HID-Fi never starts Bluetooth
GHSA-3pp8-42fh-3j3c.evidence: esp32s3 sdkconfig: no SOC_BT_CLASSIC_SUPPORTED; grep 'BLE\|esp_bt' hid_fi/ -> none

GHSA-43gh-7r4f-qp57.reason: Bluetooth Classic AVRCP: not on ESP32-S3; Bluetooth never started

GHSA-qhf9-vr2h-jh96.reason: Bluetooth Classic AVRCP: not on ESP32-S3; Bluetooth never started

GHSA-hmjj-rjvv-w8pq.reason: Bluetooth Classic SDP: not on ESP32-S3; Bluetooth never started

GHSA-v335-fxwc-rc44.reason: Bluetooth Classic L2CAP: not on ESP32-S3; Bluetooth never started

GHSA-xcpr-5mqp-9qvv.reason: Bluedroid A2DP sink (Bluetooth Classic): not on ESP32-S3; Bluetooth never started

GHSA-8mg7-9qpg-p92v.reason: ESP32 (original chip) Bluetooth controller; HID-Fi is ESP32-S3 and never starts Bluetooth
GHSA-8mg7-9qpg-p92v.evidence: advisory names the ESP32 controller; grep 'esp_bt' hid_fi/ -> none

GHSA-9j5x-rf36-54x9.reason: BLE provisioning: HID-Fi does not use WiFiProv/network provisioning

GHSA-9r76-858f-v6jh.reason: protocomm Security2 over Bluetooth: not used

GHSA-49x8-xqjg-2pjg.reason: ESP-TEE: not available on ESP32-S3 and not enabled

GHSA-v6r2-f6p2-88cj.reason: JPEG decoder: HID-Fi decodes no images

GHSA-vcw6-jc3p-4gj8.reason: ESP32-P4 hardware JPEG decoder: other chip, not used

GHSA-m2h2-683f-9mw7.reason: WPS enrollee: HID-Fi never starts WPS

RUSTSEC-2026-0387.reason: crypto-bigint 0.5.5 timing: only in the LINUX Companion (RustCrypto DTLS via dimpl -> ecdsa 0.16); macOS uses Apple crypto, Windows CNG. On Linux a DTLS handshake starts only after a valid one-use, HMAC-signed viewer ticket, so an attacker cannot collect timing samples
RUSTSEC-2026-0387.evidence: cargo tree -i crypto-bigint@0.5.5 --target {aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc}: nothing; x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu: via dimpl; DESIGN.md 'Viewer tickets'
RUSTSEC-2026-0387.revisit: move as soon as dimpl/str0m use crypto-bigint >= 0.7.6; or any DTLS path without a ticket

RUSTSEC-2026-0384.reason: tokio 1.54.0 Interval race: tokio is in Cargo.lock only through wasm-bindgen-futures (wasm targets); no native Companion build contains it
RUSTSEC-2026-0384.evidence: cargo tree -i tokio --target {aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu}: nothing

GHSA-qwgh-2vcv-g2f7.reason: block-buffer 0.10.4: needs a panic caught inside a digest's block function; sha2/hmac never panic there and the Companion's crates never call catch_unwind (str0m only in a test)
GHSA-qwgh-2vcv-g2f7.revisit: catch_unwind around hashing; move with sha2 0.11

GHSA-wrw7-89jp-8q8g.reason: glib 0.18 VariantStrIter unsoundness: Linux tray only (tray-icon -> gtk); the Companion never iterates GVariant strings
GHSA-wrw7-89jp-8q8g.revisit: tray-icon >= 0.26 drops gtk 0.18 - move with it

RUSTSEC-2024-0370.reason: proc-macro-error is unmaintained (no vulnerability); build-time macro under glib-macros, Linux only

RUSTSEC-2026-0370.reason: zvariant unmaintained notice (no vulnerability); Linux tray/notifications via zbus
RUSTSEC-2026-0370.revisit: a vulnerability in zbus, or a maintained replacement

RUSTSEC-2026-0371.reason: zbus_names unmaintained notice (no vulnerability); as RUSTSEC-2026-0370

RUSTSEC-2026-0372.reason: zvariant_derive unmaintained notice (no vulnerability); as RUSTSEC-2026-0370

GHSA-6w46-j5rx-g56g.reason: pytest < 9.0.3 /tmp/pytest-of-<user>: a local-user attack on shared UNIX machines; a development tool, not shipped; HID-Fi's tests run on single-user machines and throwaway CI runners
GHSA-6w46-j5rx-g56g.evidence: advisory text; tests/deps.json lists pytest as a minimum tool version
GHSA-6w46-j5rx-g56g.revisit: the next test-tool upgrade moves the minimum to pytest 9.0.3
